html.<b>テスターを使うなら</b>、電球のプラス端子とマイナス端子を測ります。<b: If you use a meter, measure the bulb's positive and negative terminals. 12V on both means power arrives but there's no way back; 0V on both means the fuse or the purple wire; 12V on the positive only and 0V on the negative means the bulb has blown (the voltage doesn't come through the filament).
html.<b>ドアが閉じている＝柱のボタンが押し込まれて、接点は開いています。</b>電: Door closed = the pillar button is pushed in and the contact is open. The bulb's positive terminal has 12V (the purple wire is coloured), and the voltage reaches the negative side too. It still doesn't light because both ways back are cut. Put a meter on it and you read 12V on both sides of the bulb.
html.<b>ドアを開けた＝柱のボタンが戻って、接点が閉じました。</b>人の感覚と逆に: Door opened = the pillar button springs out and the contact closes. It seems backwards, but “opening” the door turns the switch “on”. Return ② connects to ground and the bulb lights. The built-in switch stays “Off”, untouched — and it lights anyway: that's what a circuit with two ways back looks like.

The interior light's purple wire is also live with the key out. It's after the same fuse F1 as the horn = a permanent supply. Before removing the mirror and touching the wiring, disconnect the battery's negative (−) terminal.
⚠️ Leave the built-in switch “On” when you get out, and it keeps draining the battery. On a car left for a few days, this is a quiet cause of “the starter won't turn in the morning” (though how many days it takes is a matter of current, which this diagram can't show).
⚠️ When replacing the bulb, keep the same wattage. A bigger one deforms the lens and the mirror's plastic with heat.

html.<span class=\"pin-hot\">●</span>ヒューズ箱は<b: The ● fuse box is at the front of the car. Of the two purple wires leaving it, one goes to the horn at the front and the other through the roof to the mirror. The door pillar switch is on the way, in the pillar at the base of the door.
html.<span class=\"qa-h\">ドアを「開ける」と、スイッチは「入る」: “Open” the door and the switch goes “on” The door pillar switch is pushed in while the door is closed, and its contact is open. Open the door and the button pops out, closing the contact. — Pressed is “Off”, released is “On”. It's the opposite of what you'd expect, so if you mix this up when measuring with a meter, every conclusion is reversed. This diagram labels the switch by “the state of the door” (not by whether the contact is open or closed).
